rules.statement: Read an integer that a remote party sends in JSON with the `NCode.Json` whole-number readers (`TryGetWholeInt32` / `TryGetPropertyWholeInt32` on a `JsonElement`, or `WholeInt32JsonConverter` on a serialized `int` member), never with `JsonElement.TryGetInt32` or the serializer's default `int` handling.
rules.why: JSON has a single number type (RFC 8259 §6), so a sender may write 60 as `60.0` or `6e1`. The default readers reject those forms and break valid responses.
rules.check: Look for `TryGetInt32`, `GetInt32`, `TryGetValue<int>` or a plain `int`/`int?` DTO member with no `[JsonConverter(typeof(WholeInt32JsonConverter))]` that reads a number from a remote response or request, such as `expires_in`.

rules.statement: When a JSON number that should be a whole count has a non-zero fraction, is out of `int` range, or arrives as a string or another non-number kind, refuse it. Do not round, truncate or parse it from a string.
rules.why: Rounding or truncating invents a value the remote party never stated, and the RFCs specify a JSON number, not a numeric string.
rules.check: Look for `Math.Round`, `Math.Truncate`, `(int)` casts of doubles or decimals, or `int.Parse` on string-kind JSON values when reading protocol integers.

rules.statement: Use `decimal` (`TryGetDecimal` with `decimal.Truncate`), not `double`, to test whether a JSON number is a whole value.
rules.why: Binary rounding in `double` turns `60.0000000000000001` into 60 and accepts it, while `decimal` parses it exactly and refuses it.
rules.check: Look for `TryGetDouble`/`GetDouble` or `double` arithmetic used to decide whether a JSON number is an integer.

rules.statement: Put a shared parsing or validation rule in one shared `NCode.*` package that each consumer references, instead of keeping a private copy in each package or an internal helper in an `*.Abstractions` package.
rules.why: Copies of one rule drift apart, an `*.Abstractions` package holds no helper logic, and production assemblies don't use cross-assembly `InternalsVisibleTo`.
rules.check: Look for duplicated reader or converter logic across packages, helper logic added to an `*.Abstractions` project, or `InternalsVisibleTo` added so another production assembly can reach the helper.

rules.statement: Make a `TryGet...` JSON reader helper check `ValueKind` first and return `false` for any unacceptable value. It must never throw.
rules.why: The whole-number readers follow the non-throwing pattern of the existing `NumericDate` readers.
rules.check: Look for a new `TryGet*` extension on `JsonElement` that calls a throwing `Get*` method or doesn't check `ValueKind` before reading.
